Mike wants to buy a new car. He has chosen a red car for $35000. To be able to pay this price, he needs to loan part of the money from the bank, at a rate of 15%. How much money in total will Mike need to pay for the car, if he has to take $20000 from the bank?

First, we need to calculate the interest Mike will have to pay on the loan. The loan amount is $20,000 and the interest rate is 15%. The interest can be calculated as follows:

\[ \text{Interest} = 20000 \times 0.15 = 3000 \]

So, the total amount Mike will need to pay back to the bank is the loan amount plus the interest:

\[ \text{Total loan repayment} = 20000 + 3000 = 23000 \]

Next, we need to add the amount Mike is paying out of his own pocket for the car. He is paying $15,000 (since the total price of the car is $35,000 and he is borrowing $20,000).

\[ \text{Total payment} = 15000 + 23000 = 38000 \]

Therefore, the total amount Mike will need to pay for the car is $38,000.

FINAL: 38000
